summary.headline: Finkurve's Q1 FY27 AUM grew 135% YoY to a 118-branch network, with gross NPA at 0.54% and debt-to-equity up to 2.9x.
summary.overview:
Management described Q1 FY27 as a transition quarter for the gold loan industry, with new RBI norms prompting sector-wide alignment and some near-term drag on customer and channel momentum. Reported AUM rose 135% YoY, revenue about 89% YoY and PAT about 65% YoY, with branches up from 83 to 118. Asset quality was stable (gross NPA 0.54%, net NPA 0.48%), while leverage rose sharply (debt-to-equity 0.7x to 2.9x) and ROA fell to 2.9%. Management reiterated 50-60% AUM growth guidance for FY27 and disclosed the first institutional NCD subscription (Rs 50 crore from Franklin Templeton).</overview>

segments.name: Gold loans (consumption and income-generating)
segments.commentary: Average ticket size rose to Rs 1.87 lakh from Rs 1.31 lakh a year earlier; average AUM per branch is Rs 10.3 crore against a target of Rs 12-13 crore. Management attributes roughly 50% of YoY AUM growth to tonnage and 50% to gold price.

segments.name: Co-lending
segments.commentary: Co-lending share is about 3% currently; target is 15-20% of the book by end-FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 50-60% retained; management said Q1 AUM grew about 16% QoQ and that Q3 and Q4 are seasonally stronger.
Target leverage of 4x to 4.5x debt-to-equity; management does not expect to exceed 4x in FY27.
Lending yields expected to stabilise around 20-20.5%, with about 50 bps of yield improvement guided.
Cost of funds expected to fall as co-lending rises to 15-20% and as a re-rating is expected at around Rs 2,000 crore AUM; the company is rated BBB+.
Steady-state ROA target around 3%; over five years, management aspires to 3-3.5% ROA and 18% ROE.
New branches expected to break even in 12-18 months at a breakeven AUM of Rs 5-6 crore.
Rs 30 crore promoter share-warrant infusion expected by November 2026 (deadline), adding roughly Rs 100 crore of leverage headroom.
Expansion limited to current four southern states before moving to Odisha; no plans for distant regions.
capex_capacity: Branch network grew from 83 to 118 as of 30 June 2026; expansion is organic, state by state, within the four current southern states.
Leverage headroom of about Rs 1,600 crore on book plus about Rs 400 crore off book, per management, with a runway of about Rs 800 crore before optimal leverage.
Net worth about Rs 350 crore; management says this supports roughly Rs 350 crore of additional AUM, with co-lending adding Rs 300-400 crore, taking AUM to Rs 1,900-2,000 crore on current capital.
Compliance and risk functions strengthened with a new CRO and Head of Compliance; compliance software investment underway under a year-long plan.
demand_pricing: Management said the industry is seeing smaller ticket sizes, which track gold prices after a correction and higher volatility in Q1.

Competition from banks and PSUs is viewed as targeting a different, lower-yield customer segment; management says pricing is largely the same across lenders and differentiation is on product, service and post-disbursal service.
Management expects growth in new branches to continue on low-base effects, while the existing book is more exposed to gold price declines.
Management said the Q1 AUM growth was achieved despite gold price correction and the regulatory transition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target leverage range and co-lending share for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Target leverage of 4x to 4.5x, with no move beyond 4x in FY27; co-lending target of 15-20% by end-FY27 versus about 3% currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital headroom to grow further?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 1,600 crore on book plus Rs 400 crore off book; with co-lending and promoter warrants, AUM could reach Rs 1,900-2,000 crore on current capital.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company complying with RBI gold loan norms on valuation and LTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Valuation changes are limited to SMS or letter notification on valuation differences and a valuation certificate; LTV is now tiered at 85%, 80% and 75% for consumption loans, with income-generating loans underwritten under a board-approved policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for NIM and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields to stabilise around 20-20.5%, cost of funds to fall with co-lending and re-rating, and opex-to-AUM to decline with scale; ROA is currently depressed by leverage, with a steady-state target of about 3%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 135% AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 50% to tonnage and 50% to gold price; customer additions of about 1,800 per month.

qa_highlights.question: What are the branch economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Average AUM per branch is Rs 10.3 crore, targeting Rs 12-13 crore; breakeven takes 12-18 months at around Rs 5-6 crore AUM.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company compete with banks and PSUs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said banks serve a lower-yield segment, and the company competes on product, service and post-disbursal service rather than price.

risks_watch: Gold price correction and volatility could reduce ticket sizes and slow growth in the existing book, per management.
Leverage at 2.9x debt-to-equity with ROA at 2.9% and pre-tax spread of only 100-200 bps; cost of borrowing 11-11.5% against 20% yield and 6-7% opex.
Co-lending ramp from 3% to 15-20% and cost-of-funds re-rating are both needed for the margin expansion case.
Ongoing regulatory circulars every two to three weeks; management describes compliance as an evolving framework.
Promoter warrant infusion of Rs 30 crore due by November 2026.
Management declined to comment on the share price decline of about 50-55% from highs, which an analyst raised.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and guidance, but cautious on near-term momentum, which management attributed to the regulatory transition and gold price correction. Answers on competition and regulation were broad, and management declined to comment on the share price.
key_quotes: We have never believed in pursuing short -term growth at the expe nse of long -term franchise quality.
We will continue to scale the business in a manner where systems, technology, governance, and risk management remain ahead of growth.
